cases.sentence: — Ma bonne amie, je crains que le fruschtique (comme dit Фока — повар) de ce matin ne m’aie pas fait du mal.[404] — Дружочек, боюсь, чтоб от ___ (как называет его повар Фока) мне бы не было дурно.
cases.explain: «нынешнего фриштика» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Dearest, I’m afraid this morning’s fruschtique48—as Fóka the cook calls it—has disagreed with me.”

cases.sentence: (Марья Богдановна была акушерка из ___, жившая в Лысых Горах уже другую неделю.)
cases.explain: «уездного города» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: (Márya Bogdánovna was a midwife from the neighboring town, who had been at Bald Hills for the last fortnight.)

cases.sentence: — И в ___, — подхватила княжна Марья, — может быть, точно.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Oh yes,” assented Princess Márya, “perhaps that’s it. I’ll go. Courage, my angel.” She kissed Liza and was about to leave the room.

cases.sentence: — И кроме бледности, на лице ___ выразился детский страх неотвратимого физического страдания.
cases.explain: «маленькой княгини» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, no, no!” And besides the pallor and the physical suffering on the little princess’ face, an expression of childish fear of inevitable pain showed itself.

cases.sentence: — И княгиня заплакала детски-страдальчески, капризно и даже несколько притворно, ломая свои ___.
cases.explain: «маленькие ручки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “No, it’s only indigestion? … Say it’s only indigestion, say so, Marie! Say …” And the little princess began to cry capriciously like a suffering child and to wring her little hands even with some affectation. Princess Márya ran out of the room to fetch Márya Bogdánovna.

cases.sentence: Потирая полные, небольшие, белые руки, ей навстречу, с ___, уже шла акушерка.
cases.explain: «значительно-спокойным лицом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The midwife was already on her way to meet her, rubbing her small, plump white hands with an air of calm importance.

cases.sentence: Она взглянула — официанты несли для чего-то в спальню ___, стоявший в кабинете князя Андрея.
cases.explain: «кожаный диван» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Five minutes later Princess Márya from her room heard something heavy being carried by. She looked out. The men servants were carrying the large leather sofa from Prince Andréy’s study into the bedroom. On their faces was a quiet and solemn look.

cases.sentence: Несколько женщин ___ проходили туда и оттуда, оглядывались на княжну и отворачивались от нее.
cases.explain: «тихими шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Princess Márya sat alone in her room listening to the sounds in the house, now and then opening her door when someone passed and watching what was going on in the passage. Some women passing with quiet steps in and out of the bedroom glanced at the princess and turned away. She did not venture to ask any questions, and shut the door again, now sitting down in her easy chair, now taking her prayer book, now kneeling before the icon stand. To her surprise and distress she found that her prayers did not calm her excitement. Suddenly her door opened softly and her old nurse, Praskóvya Sávishna, who hardly ever came to that room as the old prince had forbidden it, appeared on the threshold with a shawl round her head.

cases.sentence: Вдруг дверь ее комнаты тихо отворилась и на пороге ее показалась повязанная платком ее ___ Прасковья Савишна, почти никогда, вследствие запрещения князя, не входившая к ней в комнату.
cases.explain: «старая няня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Princess Márya sat alone in her room listening to the sounds in the house, now and then opening her door when someone passed and watching what was going on in the passage. Some women passing with quiet steps in and out of the bedroom glanced at the princess and turned away. She did not venture to ask any questions, and shut the door again, now sitting down in her easy chair, now taking her prayer book, now kneeling before the icon stand. To her surprise and distress she found that her prayers did not calm her excitement. Suddenly her door opened softly and her old nurse, Praskóvya Sávishna, who hardly ever came to that room as the old prince had forbidden it, appeared on the threshold with a shawl round her head.

cases.sentence: ___, ступая на пятку, ходил по кабинету и послал Тихона к Марье Богдановне спросить: что́?
cases.explain: «Старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: There was no laughter in the maids’ large hall. In the men servants’ hall all sat waiting, silently and alert. In the outlying serfs’ quarters torches and candles were burning and no one slept. The old prince, stepping on his heels, paced up and down his study and sent Tíkhon to ask Márya Bogdánovna what news.—“Say only that ‘the prince told me to ask,’ and come and tell me her answer.”
